subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async resource lifecycle/shutdown API across agent, gateway, and plugin cleanup paths, and which boundary should own it?
rationale: The remaining work would create or reshape cross-boundary lifecycle contracts; source inspection shows targeted fixes exist, but no single failing path proves the shared API shape.

options.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle seam
options.body: Add a small backward-compatible drain/cancel API and prove it across one agent cleanup path plus one plugin or gateway path before broader migration.

options.title: Keep targeted lifecycle fixes
options.body: Continue fixing concrete races in their owning subsystems and close this tracker once remaining symptoms are represented by narrower issues.

options.title: Defer until another concrete race appears
options.body: Leave the current guards in place and revisit a shared API only if a new unfixed race cannot be handled by existing hooks.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Add a small backward-compatible drain/cancel API and prove it across one agent cleanup path plus one plugin or gateway path before broader migration.
